doc.title: Frank Tiberi interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 30, 2022

title: Advice to students and Charlie Parker with a plastic saxophone
summary: Advice to diversify, then the Philadelphia clubs and a story of seeing Charlie Parker playing a plastic saxophone with his leg in a cast.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: Well I would say to you know other areas in the music business actually they’d be able to focus on too also as well. I mean such as arranging and of course I mean there’s an A&R man or you know as I say always have something that you can really have on the side actually because you know it’d be pretty hard to live as a jazz player unless you are able to really get yourself a good group and a good agent and a good recording, a good CD and a lot of distribution and that takes time but it works. That’s the way that one has to really do it that way. I mean get all your things on YouTube. I mean and then you play all the clubs in New York or — there are no clubs anymore in Philadelphia. That’s a big drag. You know at that time it was the Blue Note, the Show Boat, the Pep’s Musical Bar and all that. They’re not around. That’s where — I’ll give you just — The Rendezvous I remember on Market Street actually, in the afternoon they had like some sort of a subtle jazz club. And I went in and I looked and who was sitting on a high chair was Charlie Parker and playing a plastic saxophone with his leg in a cast. I nearly fell over. I can’t believe that.
Was it an actual gig for him or was he just like —
He was up there, he was playing, yeah. Yeah. It was like it wasn’t a big showplace or anything it was just a local bar right in the center of town and here he was with a cast and a plastic saxophone.
That’s interesting because so many people, so many saxophone players did all they could to play like him but I don’t think the plastic saxophone was part of the routine.
No. But he could play anything. He could probably whistle I suppose, and sound good.
